newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs under pressure from Nikkei.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs under pressure from Nikkei.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures recovered from their lows but remained under pressure on Monday following a strong rebound on the Tokyo stock market, dealers said.

"The dollar/yen was so low this morning, we thought the Nikkei would be sold but it was only temporarily sold and then it rebounded strongly in the afternoon," a trader with a European futures house said.
He said the Nikkei's strength was likely to keep a lid on gains in Euroyen and JGB futures, as the Japanese stock and debt markets tended to move in opposite directions.
"The Euroyen and JGBs are looking bearish chart-wise. And a lot of people are saying there's no reason for Japan to keep interest rates low now," a trader with a Japanese house said.
But he said the Bank of Japan was unlikely to give up its easy monetary policy until there were clearer signs an economic recovery was well under way in Japan.
"I would suggest selling on rallies because the market looks like it's going down," he said, adding that the lead December Euroyen contract could come off to 98.81 and 98.70 eventually.
It stood at 98.87 at 1115 GMT after hitting a low of 98.85 against its IMM close at 98.86.
June JGBs settled at 123.29 against their previous 123.27.

Comments by Taku Yamasaki, a senior Liberal Democratic Party member, that it would not be possible to change Japan's record low interest rate regime without further observing the economy helped underpin the market, dealers said.
Eurodollar futures ended little changed after briefly testing the downside in thin trade. December finished at 93.725 against an IMM close at 93.720 on volume of 5,635 lots.
Dealers said the market was awaiting a slew of economic data, including U.S. April retail sales, wholesale prices, consumer prices and industrial production.
